title: BODIPY-Patatin assay proteomics
projectDescription: The potato protein patatin embeds bioactive peptides that require targeted hydrolysis to be released as promising food additives. This study presents a patatin-specific protease assay for assessing a wide range of protease activities in high-throughput format. Conjugating patatin to the amine reactive fluorogenic BODIPY FL dye provided a stable protease substrate with efficient homo-FRET quenching at a low degree (7-8) of labeling. Compared to commercial BODIPY-casein, BODIPY-patatin provided higher fluorescence enhancement (by de-quenching) at high protease concentrations, while the sensitivity was generally comparable for both highly specific (e.g. Trypsin) and industrial relevant proteases (e.g. Alcalase and Neutrase) at low doses. For Chymotrypsin, BODIPY-patatin provided a 39% response improvement at 5 ng dose. Peptide-centric mass spectrometry analyses identified several BODIPY-labeling sites with varying occupancies in patatin, indicating heterogenous labeling under the applied conjugation conditions. BODIPY-labeled patatin complements commercial BODIPY-labeled casein as a globular, plant-based alternative for screening of proteolytic activity.
sampleProcessingProtocol: The BODIPY FL patatin conjugate (BODIPY-patatin) was synthesized by conjugating purified native patatin with the amine reactive dye BODIPY FL succinimidyl (NHS) ester (Thermo Fisher). The conjugation was performed with 4 mg BODIPY FL NHS in 200 µL dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO). The probe solution was dropwise mixed with 8.0 mg patatin (10 mg/mL) in 0.12 M NaHCO3 buffer pH 8.3 according to manufacturer guidelines. The conjugation reaction was performed for 2 h at room temperature in darkness on a roller mixer with occasional vortexing. The reaction was stopped by adding 400 µL 1.5 M hydroxylamine and incubating for 1 h at room temperature in the dark. BODIPY-patatin was separated from the unreacted labeling reagent on a Sephadex 25 PD-10 Desalting gravity column (GE healthcare, United Kingdom) equilibrated in 0.1 M NaHCO3 pH 8.4. The total sample volume of 1.4 mL was loaded and entered the column bed completely before 1 mL equilibration buffer was loaded to adjust the sample volume. The elution step was carried out with 3.5 mL 0.1 M NaHCO3 pH 8.4.  The six collected elution fractions were analyzed using 4-20% gradient sodium dodecyl-sulfate (SDS) polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (PAGE) gels (GenScript, USA) under reducing condition (60 mM dithiothreitol (DTT)), according to manufacturer. Protein samples (~10 µg protein) were mixed with reducing SDS sample buffer, and incubated for 5 min at 95 °C (Gregersen et al., 2021). Gels were loaded with 10 µL of molecular weight markers for either Coomassie Brilliant Blue G250 staining, (Unstained Protein MW Marker (Thermo Scientific)) or fluorescent imagining (Precision Plus Protein™ Dual Xtra Prestained Protein Standard (Bio-Rad)). Gels were visualized using a ChemiDoc MP Imaging System (Bio-Rad, USA). Based on the SDS-PAGE analysis, elution fractions with purified BODIPY-patatin were pooled to a standard stock solution. The BODIPY FL casein conjugate (BODIPY-casein) was applied from the EnzChek Protease Assay Kit (ThermoFishe Scientific) and prepared as stated by the manufacturer. Stock solutions of both BODIPY-patatin and BODIPY-casein were aliquoted and stored at -80 °C until use.   BODIPY-patatin and unconjugated patatin were digested with Alcalase or Trypsin for analysis by LC-MS/MS. The proteolytic digestions were gently mixed in Eppendorf tubes and had a reaction volume of 0.200 mL, containing 6.5 µg/mL protease substrate and 0.5 µg/mL protease in 10 mM Tris pH 7.4. The reaction time began with the addition of the protease as the last component. The reactions incubated in an air incubator at 37 °C for 10 min, 30 min, and 60 min. The proteolytic reactions were stopped by heating the samples to 95 °C for 5 min on a heating block and subsequently snap freezing in liquid nitrogen. The thawed digestion mixtures were not further hydrolyzed but mixed with detergent-containing buffer for protein denaturation, followed by reduction of disulfide bonds and cysteine alkylation, as previously described (Jafarpour et al., 2020). Alkylated peptide samples were desalted using in-house prepared C-18 StageTips (Rappsilber et al., 2007) and dried on a vacuum concentrator. Peptides were resuspended in 0.1% (v/v) formic acid, 2% (v/v) acetonitrile for analysis, using automated Liquid Chromatography-Electrospray Ionization-tandem Mass Spectrometry (LC-ESI-MS/MS), as previously described (Gregersen et al., 2021). In brief, approximately 1 µg peptide was separated on a C18 PEPMAP (Thermo Scientific) nano column by an EASY nLC-1200 over a 60 minute gradient and injected into a Q Exactive HF mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific). The MS was operated in positive mode and employed a top 20 data dependent acquisition strategy, scanning precursor ions in the range 400-1200 m/z at a 60,000 resolution followed by HCD fragmentation (28 eV) and MS/MS spectral scanning at a resolution of 15,000. Maximum injection time was 50 ms for MS and 45 ms for MS/MS scans. The underfill ratio was set to 3.5% and a dynamic exclusion of 30 sec was defined. “Peptide match” and “exclude isotopes” were enabled during acquisition.
dataProcessingProtocol: Proteomics and peptidomics analyses were performed using MaxQuant 2.2.0.0 , and data was initially searched against a curated sequence database from potato (S. tuberosum). The analyses were carried out as specific and unspecific digestions for the Trypsin and Alcalase samples, respectively. In the tryptic analysis, a minimal peptide length of six was applied, whereas in the unspecific Alcalase analysis, peptides ranging in length from 5 to 35 amino acids were included. The specific tryptic analysis employed a 1% false discovery rate (FDR), while the unspecific analysis of Alcalase data employed a 10% FDR on both peptide and protein level. In both analyses, match between runs and dependent peptides (1% FDR) were enabled. Cysteine carbamidomethylation was defined as a fixed modification, while methionine oxidation, N-terminal alkylation, and BODIPY FL (+C14H13OBF2N2, Δm = 274.1089 Da) on both protein N-terminal and lysine side chains were defined as variable modifications (up to 5 per peptide). Prior to further analysis, peptides identified as reverse hits or contaminants were removed from the peptide datasets. As the majority of peptides (qualitatively and quantitatively) were ascribed to the twelve patatin isoforms, the LC-MS/MS raw data was subsequently searched in MaxQuant again against a protein database comprising only the sequences of these. Settings were maintained with the exception of increasing FDR to 100% due to the small database. As FDR with substantially increased, identified peptides were manually inspected and identifications with a posterior error probability (PEP) > 0.01 were removed. Relative molar protein distribution was estimated by riBAQ and ILrel for Trypsin and Alcalase hydrolysates, respectively. Based on the MaxQuant output from the search against the small database, peptide profiles from LC-MS/MS data were visualized using Peptigram . Furthermore, the occupancy of BODIPY-labeling sites was estimated based on relative peptide abundances, which was defined as the normalized intensity of a peptide in BODIPY-patatin samples relative to the same peptide in unlabeled patatin samples at the same time point. The peptide intensity normalization was performed using a representative peptide in all compared samples. The representative peptide should have a high abundance in all compared samples and not interfere with BODIPY-labeling. As such, it should not contain Lys residues in the sequence or at neighboring amino acid positions. Based on these criteria, the peptides EFLEGQLQ and HSQNNYLR were used for normalization validation in the peptide-centric analyses of the Alcalase and Trypsin datasets, respectively. Normalized intensities less than 0.001 (<0.1%) in unlabeled patatin samples were discarded.  To gain further insight into BODIPY-labeling, an extra unspecific search was carried out for the Alcalase data with modified settings. From the search parameters outlined above, the following changes were applied: FDR for modification site identification was increased to 10%, peptide length range was expanded to cover peptides from 3 to 40 amino acids, minimum score for modified peptides was reduced from 40 to 1, and a fragmented (following neutral loss of HF) BODIPY FL [[BODIPY FL] - HF] was defined (+C14H12OBFN2, Δm = 254.1027 Da) as a variable modification on both protein N-terminus and Lys, based on previous reports. In a final search, Alcalase data was processed with the same parameters, but site FDR was increased to 100%. Due to the high FDR applied in these analyses, identified peptides were manually inspected for PEP and Andromeda score before further processing.  The dataset includes twelwe raw datafiles (Thermo .raw format) six different MaxQuant serch outputs, where the unspecific serach aginst the twelwe patatin isoform database (included in the repository) on Alcalase hydrolysates serves as the main MaxQuant output dataset. The repository also includes the following searches in compressed libraries:  Trypsin_full: A 1% FDR specific/tryptic search on the Trypsin hydrolysates aginst the curated potato protein DB (included in repository). Trypsin_small: A 100% FDR specific/tryptic search on the Trypsin hydrolysates aginst the patatin isoform DB. Alcalase_full: A 10% FDR unspecific search on the Alcalase hydrolysates aginst the curated potato protein DB Alcalase_small: A 100% FDR unspecific search on the Alcalase hydrolysates aginst the patatin isoform DB (The main dataset) Alcalase_small_BODIPY_site10: A 100% FDR unspecific search on the Alcalase hydrolysates aginst the patatin isoform DB. Site FDR increased to 10% and the additional modification (BODIPY with [HF] loss) included as variable modification on Lys and N-term. Alcalase_small_BODIPY_site100: A 100% FDR unspecific search on the Alcalase hydrolysates aginst the patatin isoform DB. Site FDR increased to 100% and the additional modification (BODIPY with [HF] loss) included as variable modification on Lys and N-term.
